mood.summary: Fear is still running high. On Nov 5 the S&P 500 fell 4.4% and the Nasdaq slid into a correction, the worst day since April 2025, on worries that election results will slow AI and data-centre spending. The Fear & Greed index sits in Extreme Fear at 20, and bearish individual investors outnumber bulls by about 14 points. Stocks are bouncing on Nov 6 after a strong jobs report (165,000 jobs vs about 60,000 expected), but that also firmed bets on a December Fed rate hike.

trending.note: Board as of Wednesday 4:05 PM ET; prices are the 2026-11-25 close. Why-it's-trending notes summarize the Stocktwits stream and the news it links to.

items.name: SpaceX
items.about: SpaceX builds and launches Falcon and Starship rockets and runs the Starlink satellite internet service.
items.why: SpaceX shares swung widely, falling as low as $113.93 before recovering to close up about 1.3% at $127.39, on a day when the broader market sold off early and then bounced. The stock is still below its $135 June 2026 IPO price, and traders kept comparing its valuation with Anthropic's newly listed shares. No company-specific news drove the move.

items.name: Viking Therapeutics
items.about: Viking Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biotech developing VK2735, an injectable and oral GLP-1/GIP drug for obesity.
items.why: Viking rose about 6.5% to close near its high of the day at $31.39, its third straight gain, after presenting VK2735 data at ObesityWeek (Nov 14-17) and starting a Phase 3 program for the oral version of the drug earlier in November. No new press release came out today. Posts say partnership news could be coming, but nothing confirms that.

items.name: Ambarella
items.about: Ambarella designs low-power AI vision chips used in security cameras, car driver-assistance systems and robots.
items.why: Ambarella fell about 19.8% to $35.67 after its fiscal Q3 report on Tuesday, Nov 24. Posts say a weak forecast caused the drop, and the shares bounced well off the day's $30.51 low. Message volume ran at an extreme level, and posts say a takeover is possible, but nothing has been announced.

items.name: BitMine Immersion
items.about: BitMine Immersion is a company that holds ether as its main treasury asset, and it also runs bitcoin mining operations.
items.why: BitMine rose about 2% to $13.45, recovering from an $11.74 low as crypto-linked stocks bounced late in the day. The company reported holding about 6.08 million ETH as of Nov 15, close to its goal of owning 5% of the ether supply. Posts also shared new CFTC guidance on how platforms can count crypto reserves.

items.name: Deere & Co
items.about: Deere & Company makes John Deere farm, construction and forestry equipment and provides financing for it.
items.why: Deere reported fiscal Q4 results before the open. A MarketBeat earnings link shared on Stocktwits says EPS was $3.89, below the $4.03 estimate, on $12.12B of revenue. The stock fell to $582 early, then reversed to close up about 4.5% at $641.27. Posts say fiscal 2027 net income guidance is $4.50B-$5.25B, which assumes a modest recovery in large ag.

items.name: Anthropic
items.about: Anthropic is an AI company that builds the Claude family of large language models and sells access to them to businesses and consumers.
items.why: Anthropic shares listed on Nasdaq on Nov 19 after the IPO priced at $83. They opened at $111.50 and have since slid back to about the IPO price. Today they ranged from $73.86 to $85.92, then closed up about 1.1% at $82.85, slightly below $83, as the AI trade sold off and then recovered. Volume was heavy at about 220M shares.

items.name: Direxion Daily Semiconductor Bull 3X ETF
items.about: SOXL is a leveraged ETF that aims to deliver three times the daily return of an index of US semiconductor stocks.
items.why: SOXL fell as low as $24.61 early in the day, then recovered about 30% to close down only about 1.8% at $32.02. Chip stocks have been under pressure in November, as congressional scrutiny of Nvidia over chip exports to China erased Nvidia's 2026 gains. More than 500M shares traded.

items.name: Barrick Mining
items.about: Barrick Mining is one of the world's largest gold and copper miners.
items.why: Barrick rose about 2.9% to $34.54 as gold miners rebounded. Earlier this month the company filed an S-1 to list its North American gold assets as American Barrick (ticker ABGC) on the NYSE, and it plans to return the proceeds to shareholders. Posts also discussed a $26.40 tender offer that Barrick is urging holders to reject, but this was not confirmed.

items.name: Strive Inc
items.about: Strive is an asset manager that also holds bitcoin as a treasury asset, funded mainly through perpetual preferred stock.
items.why: Strive gained about 5.2% to $14.93 as bitcoin-linked stocks bounced from their lows. The company last disclosed about 27,460 BTC in late September. Bitcoin has slid in November, and posts noted a large share of supply now sitting at a loss. No new company announcement was found.

items.name: Lyft
items.about: Lyft runs a ride-hailing network in the US and Canada and also operates bike and scooter rentals.
items.why: Lyft rose about 5.1% to $16.96 as money moved out of tech into other sectors and the broader market recovered from an early selloff. No company-specific catalyst was found. Posts mention a pending $272.5M California driver-misclassification settlement.

items.name: KraneShares CSI China Internet ETF
items.about: KWEB is an ETF that holds China-based internet and e-commerce companies listed in the US and Hong Kong.
items.why: KWEB closed up about 0.2% at $21.20, bouncing from a $20.44 low that posts describe as a 52-week low. Posts point to Meituan's earnings on Friday and possible Beijing stimulus in December. Holdings like Alibaba were supported by strong AI cloud growth last week, while US chip-export scrutiny weighed on sentiment.

items.name: Peloton
items.about: Peloton sells connected fitness equipment such as bikes and treadmills, along with subscription workout classes.
items.why: Peloton edged up about 0.8% to $5.69. On Nov 23 its board approved a $300M share buyback, after the company completed a refinancing on Nov 20. The refinancing raised $700M of 8.625% notes due 2032, paid off its $1B term loan and added a $200M revolver.

items.name: Alibaba (ADR)
items.about: Alibaba runs China's largest e-commerce platforms and the Alibaba Cloud computing business.
items.why: Alibaba gained about 1.6% to close near its high of the day at $86.25, still riding its Nov 19 report, in which AI cloud revenue grew 53% to about 61B yuan and total revenue rose 10% to 271.5B yuan. The stock is still under pressure from reports of ties to Megaspeed, a Singapore firm under US export-control investigation. Posts mention a securities lawsuit over this.

items.name: VanEck Gold Miners ETF
items.about: GDX is an ETF that holds large gold mining companies from around the world.
items.why: GDX rose about 3.5% to $73.87 after a sharp intraday turnaround from a $67.93 low. Posts say miners were deeply oversold after weeks of selling. The Dec 8 Fed meeting is the next macro event traders are watching for gold.

items.name: Lufax ADR
items.about: Lufax is a Chinese consumer and small-business lending platform backed by Ping An.
items.why: Lufax rose about 2.6% to $6.39 after touching $5.86, even though rival Qifu's earnings and guidance disappointed on Tuesday. Posts argue that Lufax's consumer-finance and banking licenses could help it under China's tighter lending rules, while others expect more pressure on the sector. No Lufax-specific news was found.

items.name: Carnival
items.about: Carnival is the world's largest cruise operator, with brands such as Carnival, Princess and AIDA.
items.why: Carnival slipped about 1.4% to $27.99 as travel stocks dropped early in the session. Posts say a new attack on a Saudi pipeline could push fuel costs higher. Saudi Arabia did shut its East-West pipeline after drone attacks in September, but I could not confirm a new incident today.

items.name: Netskope
items.about: Netskope sells cloud-based network security software (SASE/SSE) that protects how companies access the web and cloud apps.
items.why: Netskope rose about 3.5% to $26.43 and broke above the $26 level it had failed to clear before. Security stocks drew interest after reports of breaches at the CIA and FBI. The company reports fiscal Q3 results on Dec 2, and BTIG raised its price target to $30 on Nov 3. Posts say a takeover is possible, but nothing supports that.

items.name: HP Inc
items.about: HP Inc makes personal computers, printers and printing supplies.
items.why: HP jumped about 11.4% to $31.12, one of the few tech gainers on the day, after its fiscal Q4 report. Posts say revenue was about $16B (up 9%) and adjusted EPS was $0.83 against about $0.75 expected. They also say AI PCs reached nearly 60% of shipments, the dividend went up to $0.31, and FY2027 EPS guidance is $3.15-$3.45. I could not confirm these figures in a web search.

items.name: Sanofi ADR
items.about: Sanofi is a French drugmaker known for the immunology blockbuster Dupixent, vaccines and specialty medicines.
items.why: Sanofi rose about 4.8% to a 52-week high of $54.38 after agreeing to buy Insmed for $175 per share in cash, about $41B. That is roughly a 46% premium to Insmed's unaffected price, and the deal adds a new growth driver ahead of Dupixent's patent expiry. Posts say RBC, Barclays and BofA upgraded the stock after the deal.

items.name: Axon Enterprise
items.about: Axon Enterprise makes TASER devices, body cameras and cloud evidence software for police and public-safety agencies.
items.why: Axon rose about 7.5% to $343.19 after a roughly $40 swing from the day's $304.26 low, adding to gains from the previous session. No company-specific news was found. Traders on the board were asking what triggered the move.
